basis: Expected values for the lexical row csharp-B01 and the type-name row csharp-B02, derived without any native output. An alternative is EXPECTED with witnesses (spans of the pinned Roslyn observation, accepted sources linked to the alternative by the ledger, at most one per case and three in all) and the tree-sitter node types the pinned grammar allows, or BLOCKED with a reason code. basis spec-derived: the lexeme or lexical form comes from the ECMA-334 lexical grammar as published in the C# standard draft v13 on learn.microsoft.com (clauses in the spec field) and Roslyn only locates it; basis differential-oracle: the structure is what the pinned Roslyn DLLs observed, translated by the kind map. match span: a node of one of the types spans exactly [start,end); starts-at: a node of one of the types starts at start. The cross_check section compares every observed token and directive with the spec derivation; its mismatches are dispositions, not adopted values. The sections audit and metamorphic record the specification sample audit and the metamorphic check. The single-oracle limit applies: a differential-oracle expectation is the behavior of one Roslyn build, not the specification.

corrections.reason: The specification defines the symbol of #define and #undef as PP_Conditional_Symbol, a lexeme, and names no tree-sitter type. The pinned grammar text builds preproc_define and preproc_undef from the directive and one preproc_arg token, which runs to the end of the line, and has no identifier rule in them (identifier appears only in the #if and #elif condition). The witness is the symbol DEBUG of '#define DEBUG' followed directly by the line end, so the token has the witness's span.

corrections.reason: The specification makes Interpolated_Regular_String_Start one lexeme of two characters ($"). The pinned grammar text has no node of that extent: interpolated_string_expression begins with two nodes, an interpolation_start (an alias of the external token interpolation_regular_start) and then a quote node. The grammar text does not give the extent of the external token, so only the start is derivable: an interpolation_start node starts where the lexeme starts.

The specification makes Interpolated_Verbatim_String_Start one lexeme ($@" or @$"). The pinned grammar text begins the verbatim form with an interpolation_start (an alias of the external token interpolation_verbatim_start) and then a quote node, so no node has the lexeme's extent, and only the start is derivable: an interpolation_start node starts where the lexeme starts.

Same lexeme class and grammar rule as csharp-B01.a396: the verbatim start @$" is one lexeme in the specification and begins with an interpolation_start (alias of interpolation_verbatim_start) followed by a quote node in the pinned grammar text, so only the start is derivable.

The ts of this differential-oracle alternative, interpolation_start, was translated from the kind map r1 entry of its Roslyn kind. It stays interpolation_start because the pinned grammar text begins the interpolated string with an interpolation_start node (an alias of the external token interpolation_regular_start): the basis of the ts is that grammar text.

non_array_type: pointer_type is the pointer type as the element type of an array type (8.2.1; 24.3.2 lists int*[] as an array of pointers to int). The old witness is the type of the field 'int* p' (24-28), which is the instance of type: pointer_type (a008) and not of this alternative. The instance here is the element type 'int*' of 'int*[] arr' (62-66): the pinned grammar text lets array_type take a pointer_type as its base, and a pointer_type covers 'int*' exactly. The Roslyn observation holds a PointerType at 62-66.

unmanaged_type: pointer_type is the pointer type as the operand of sizeof (8.8; 12.8.19 sizeof_expression takes an unmanaged_type). The old witness is the type of the field 'int* p' (24-28), the instance of type: pointer_type (a008). The instance here is the operand 'int*' of 'sizeof(int*)' (211-215): the pinned grammar text gives sizeof_expression a type field and a pointer_type covers 'int*' exactly. The Roslyn observation holds a PointerType at 211-215.

nullable_type_annotation is the token '?' (8.2.1, 6.4.6). The old witness is the nullable type 'int?' (86-90), a node that contains the instance. In the pinned grammar text the '?' is an anonymous token of nullable_type, so the token '?' (89-90, Roslyn QuestionToken) is the exact witness and its type is the anonymous token '"?"', the type the kind map r2 gives QuestionToken.

type_parameter_constraints is the constraint list of a where clause (15.2.5). The old witness is the whole clause 'where T : class' (66-81), a node that contains the instance. The pinned grammar text has no node for the list: the clause is 'where', an identifier, ':' and a comma separated list of type_parameter_constraint nodes. In this source the list holds one constraint, so the instance is that constraint, 'class' (76-81, Roslyn ClassConstraint), which has the extent of the list. The witness therefore proves a single constraint list only; a list of several constraints is not shown.

ref_kind: 'ref' is the keyword ref of a parameter (15.6.1). The old witness is the whole parameter 'ref int a' (31-40), a node that contains the instance. The pinned grammar text makes every parameter modifier keyword its own modifier node, so the exact witness is the keyword 'ref' (31-34, Roslyn RefKeyword), typed as the anonymous token and the modifier node the kind map r2 gives RefKeyword.

parameter_modifier: parameter_mode_modifier is a ref, out or in keyword on a parameter (15.6.2.1). The old witness is the whole parameter 'ref int a' (31-40), a node that contains the instance. The pinned grammar text makes each such keyword its own modifier node, so the exact witness is the keyword 'ref' (31-34, Roslyn RefKeyword), typed as the kind map r2 types RefKeyword.

The pinned grammar text makes the keyword its own modifier node, so the exact witness is 'ref' (31-34, Roslyn RefKeyword), typed as the kind map r2 types RefKeyword.

parameter_mode_modifier: 'out' is the keyword out of a parameter (15.6.2.1). The old witness is the whole parameter 'out int b' (42-51), a node that contains the instance. The pinned grammar text makes the keyword its own modifier node, so the exact witness is 'out' (42-45, Roslyn OutKeyword), typed as the kind map r2 types OutKeyword.

parameter_mode_modifier: 'in' is the keyword in of a parameter (15.6.2.1). The old witness is the whole parameter 'in int c' (53-61), a node that contains the instance. The pinned grammar text makes the keyword its own modifier node, so the exact witness is 'in' (53-55, Roslyn InKeyword), typed as the kind map r2 types InKeyword.

The specification's regular_interpolation is the expression, alignment and format between the braces; the braces are terminals of the enclosing rule. The pinned grammar text builds the interpolation node with an interpolation_brace first child (an alias of the external token interpolation_open_brace) and one last (an alias of interpolation_close_brace). The node therefore starts at the opening brace and ends with the closing brace; the grammar text does not give the extent of an external token, so only the start is derivable (the principle of csharp-B01.a383): an interpolation node starts where its opening brace starts.

Same node and grammar rule as csharp-B01.a381 for a verbatim interpolated string: the verbatim string content uses the same interpolation rule, whose first and last children are aliases of the external tokens interpolation_open_brace and interpolation_close_brace, so only the start of the node is derivable.
